posts.post_subject: Reference Beam Single Beam Set Up
posts.content_md:
I have a question.

This morning I was setting up a single beam hologram. I added side lighting to each side.

While exposing I noticed the light was attenuated hitting the object (using blue light). So my question is, is the reference beam the light that strikes the plate or is it the light that transmits through the plate? Or in the middle of the film? 

If it is the light that is transmitted through the plate then wouldn't it be better to use a blue laser, and higher DiAm concentrations to attinuate the reference beam and use side lighting to increase the object light, hence getting closer than 1:1 ratio.

Hope you all have a great weekend 

Tony

posts.author: Danny Bee
posts.post_subject: Reference Beam Single Beam Set Up
posts.content_md:
hi Tony 

in single beam hologram the (refrence Beam) is the light going through the plate to the object. if you use higher DiAm concentrations in 458nm the amout of light would be attinuate. if you use the light spilling around the plate as your main light and refect that back to object and use the light going through the plate as your fill light yes you could do that in 458nm.

in green the DiAm concentrations do not attinuate that light going thro the plate as much so higher DiAm concentrations would work to your advantage. 

now in a 2 beam setup that rule doesnot aply (refections or tranmission) and you can have higher concentrations of DiAm in 458nm

lets say your where doing a head (face) right side like would be the main 1(200mw) left fill(150mw) the light going thro the plate 100mw (light reading on object side of the plate).

so at the plate you would have 1-1to 1-2 remember the light reflecting from the object would be from 50% to 80% depending on the object so if the main is 200 then the reflection for the main off the object would be 100 so it matchs your refrence and your left fill would be 75 and refection from thought the plate would be 50 sooooo it would give you 100, 75 , 50.....nice

> **Dutchelm05:** Just was thinking it would be good to use blue, increase AmDi and use the over flow light to illuminate the object.Theorically, you should get near one to one if you balance out right, no?

yes its easily acheavable to reach a one to one ratio,using thruput light or overspill light, the trick is to overlap your bounceback light, by having as many "kicker" beams overlapping light onto your object as possible........

the picture shows how i grab unused light (befor it hits the collimater) and redirect the unused light (overlapping as much as possible) the light is additive , a little here and a little there and now you reach a one to one ratio.
